sweeps.title: NVLink Fusion may keep NVIDIA in the rack when customers choose custom chips

findings.reason: NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom announced that Rebellions plans to connect its R200 NPU using NVIDIA NVLink Fusion and MGX while SK Telecom plans Korean data-centre deployments. This is a proposed integration, not proof of realised sales, inference efficiency or an event-window share-price move.
findings.sourceName: NVIDIA Newsroom — original NVLink Fusion collaboration
findings.nextCheck: Verify R200 deployments, independent cost-per-token benchmarks, SK Telecom capacity and NVIDIA networking revenue disclosures.

sweeps.title: Warm US gas storage contrasts with costly international LNG

findings.reason: EIA's 10 November outlook raised forecast end-November US storage to 3,840 Bcf (+67 Bcf) and lowered the November–March Henry Hub price forecast to $2.87/MMBtu (−16% versus the previous forecast). These are forecasts, not actual storage measurements or a current spot quote.
findings.nextCheck: Check subsequent weekly EIA storage, temperatures, matched-date Henry Hub versus TTF/JKM quotes and LNG exports.

findings.reason: The EIA reports that October monthly front-month TTF futures averaged $28.51/MMBtu and the Japan–Korea Marker $28.59/MMBtu, up from $11.27 and $10.82 respectively in February. October international futures must not be compared as a same-day spread against the November–March Henry Hub forecast.
findings.sourceName: EIA — international LNG observations in November STEO
findings.nextCheck: Retrieve matched observation dates and contract horizons before quantifying the US versus overseas gas arbitrage.

findings.reason: EIA revised its 2027 US retail diesel forecast from $4.49 to $5.03 per gallon because it sees persistent global refined-fuel constraints. This is a forecast revision, not a rise in the current pump price.
findings.nextCheck: Track ULSD cracks, refinery utilisation, distillate inventories and Hormuz vessel flow separately from Henry Hub.

sweeps.title: Iran denies active talks while US avoids new strikes

findings.reason: Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei publicly said no active US–Iran negotiations were underway and the seven demands for opening Hormuz remain unmet. Reported positions must not be conflated with a verified failure of Qatar-mediated contacts.
findings.nextCheck: Check direct Iranian/US/Qatari position, actual proposals, and whether all parties have agreed to and implemented terms.

findings.reason: Rezaei threatened retaliation against US bases in Europe if aircraft from them were used to strike Iran. This is an attributed conditional threat, not a confirmed new strike in Europe.
findings.sourceName: AFP via RTÉ — Iranian security warning
findings.nextCheck: Distinguish official threat changes from UK aircraft movement, UKMTO incidents, actual engagement and verified navigational effects.

findings.reason: Reuters reports Gulf traffic and LNG exports have recovered somewhat while attacks continue; the October counts are 31 LNG tanker departures and 37 ships attacked. They are period-specific claims, not evidence that insured commercial passage is normal.
findings.nextCheck: Confirm source denominators, incident identities, comparable prewar traffic, actual cargo volumes and marine insurance before declaring peace or normalisation.

sweeps.title: ORLEN's QatarEnergy cancellation proves disruption costs are real

findings.reason: ORLEN terminated one of two QatarEnergy long-term LNG deals on 10 Nov over prolonged force majeure. It covers 1 million tonnes a year, worth about EUR 570m in 2026 and remains legally in effect another 60 days; its second Qatari contract continues. This documents a commercial consequence, not new supply bought from Venture Global.
findings.nextCheck: Read VG and ORLEN's own contracts and actual deliveries before assigning displaced volumes or earnings benefits to VG.

findings.reason: Reuters reports the Polish buyer already receives some Venture Global US LNG. The existing supply link is a beneficiary hypothesis, not proof of incremental revenue because of this cancellation.
findings.nextCheck: Quantify replacement cargo needs, VG contracted versus spot capacity and 2027–28 margins, using original issuer filings.

sweeps.title: Nvidia's CEO decision risk is distinct from AI demand

findings.reason: Nvidia's independent directors announced on 10 Nov the retention of outside legal counsel for a formal investigation. This is an issuer-confirmed governance milestone; the release neither announced a CEO removal nor said any national-security breach was established.
findings.nextCheck: Monitor the next official board/SEC disclosure and any genuine change to the CEO role; do not treat report or betting odds as a board vote.

findings.reason: Reuters on 11 Nov reported the board was preparing to consider Huang's removal, citing WSJ; Reuters could not independently verify the allegation. Reuters' same-day global markets coverage put NVDA +2.9% in cash trading and roughly -8% after hours, not the video's unverified +6%/-10% figures.
findings.nextCheck: Check exact NVDA cash/after-hours instrument and timestamp, upcoming earnings, chip shipment/guidance and the board's next statement.

findings.reason: The claimed $28.1m EWY Jan-2028 145-strike call purchase was not independently verified from timestamped trade/OPRA data. A large options print by itself does not establish buyer identity or a naked bullish memory-chip bet.
findings.nextCheck: Locate exact trade print, premiums, opening interest, bid/ask execution and any paired legs before treating the claim as institutional conviction.

sweeps.title: Goolsbee links AI infrastructure demand with stubborn service inflation

findings.reason: In the original 10 Nov PBS interview, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee called the CPI report 'borderline disturbing', highlighting persistent services prices and data-centre spending as a source of demand-driven overheating. He did not announce an FOMC decision or a December vote.
findings.nextCheck: Test services CPI/PPI, electrical equipment costs and policy futures with source dates; separate his comments from his voting status.

findings.reason: A quoted 11.8% probability of a 50bp December move must be tied to its exact FedWatch contract, as-of timestamp and implied-probability convention. A video quote without contract cannot be a live Fed pricing feed.
findings.sourceName: CME Group — FedWatch methodology and current tool
findings.nextCheck: Read exact FedWatch 8–9 Dec 2026 distribution with time, contract and assumptions; don't copy a snapshot odds as real time.

sweeps.title: Navigation threat persists despite energy-flow recovery

findings.reason: Reuters reports, citing three sources, an alleged strike on navigation systems on Oman's Didamar island on 11 November. Damage and operational consequences were not independently verified; this is a security lead, not proof that commercial shipping stopped.
findings.nextCheck: Recover dated Omani/UKMTO notices and maritime operator reports; test whether vessel routes and completed transits actually changed.

findings.reason: EIA assesses Middle East crude-production shut-ins at about 2.5 million barrels/day in October, versus 10.9 million at the May peak. It also describes ship-to-ship transfers off Oman supporting recovered exports. Those are regional supply estimates, not a verified safe reopening of Hormuz.
findings.sourceName: EIA — November STEO crude market review
findings.nextCheck: Compare daily and completed-week commercial transits, cargo loadings, insurance and alternate-route volumes with the EIA's vintage; keep crude flow distinct from AIS crossing counts.

sweeps.title: Oil-price relief does not imply finished-fuel relief

findings.reason: EIA forecasts Brent near $100/barrel in November–December after lower October production shut-ins, but says shipping risks, longer routes and constrained tanker capacity remain. This is a November 5 forecast vintage published November 10, not a live price or proof about diesel.
findings.nextCheck: Check actual delivered crude, freight and insurance against dated Brent/WTI and separately measure diesel cracks and distillate stocks.

findings.reason: Reuters' 11 November oil report described Brent at $92.20/barrel at 01:19 GMT following a two-month low, alongside renewed ship-attack concerns. The intraday quote must not be compared as a same-period observation with EIA's monthly Brent forecast.
findings.sourceName: Reuters via Investing.com — 11 November oil tape
findings.nextCheck: Use a matched futures settlement and US/Asian product-crack observations; distinguish oil risk-premium change from physical-product shortages.

sweeps.title: Hot CPI and decent jobs are not the full growth story

findings.reason: BLS says October CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month and core rose 0.3%. Energy rose 0.7% and shelter 0.3%. Most October 2026 twelve-month CPI comparisons are unavailable because BLS did not collect October 2025 data.
findings.nextCheck: Track comparable monthly services/shelter inflation and December policy-market pricing without fabricating missing year-on-year rates.

findings.reason: BLS October employment report shows +165,000 payrolls and 4.1% unemployment; long-term unemployment stood at about 2 million, 27.6% of unemployed workers, while professional/business services added 70,000. Headline hiring and labour quality require separate evaluation.
findings.nextCheck: Compare sector job gains and losses, U-6, hours, involuntary part-time employment, wages and employment revisions in a labour-quality report.

sweeps.title: Duration and risk assets diverge after inflation surprise

findings.reason: Reuters reported that after 10 November CPI the US 2-year yield rose 18.44bp to about 4.731% and the 10-year rose 12.55bp to about 4.988%; these are dated 10 November observations, not present-time Treasury levels.
findings.nextCheck: Measure 11 November 2Y/10Y/30Y official closes, real yields, TLT and duration ETF reaction with exact dates; inspect policy-path versus term-premium explanations.

findings.reason: BLS's monthly headline +0.4% and core +0.3% establish a hotter CPI observation; they do not establish that a December 50bp hike will occur or that long bonds must keep falling.
findings.nextCheck: Separate the official release from the next-meeting implied path and investigate nominal-versus-real yield divergence.

sweeps.title: AI stock rebound challenges a one-way duration selloff

findings.reason: Associated Press reported a 11 November US equity rebound: S&P 500 about +1.3% and Nasdaq about +1.6%, with AI-related shares recovering. This is a dated session report, not evidence of a sustained new AI Regime.
findings.nextCheck: Compare 10 November selloff against 11–12 November follow-through, SMH/QQQ, 2Y/10Y yields, relative strength and cash-session breadth.

findings.reason: AP reported CoreWeave rose about 24.7% after results, revised revenue guidance and expected customer prepayments/deposits. Reporting needs verification against the actual issuer release before interpreting contracted revenue or cash conversion as established.
findings.sourceName: Associated Press — CoreWeave and AI shares
findings.nextCheck: Read CoreWeave's original 10-Q/earnings release, separate deposits from recognised revenue, calculate operating cash flow, capex, financing and FCF before any AI-funding verdict.

sweeps.title: Risk-on rebound needs equal-weight and sector confirmation

findings.reason: AP's 11 November headline S&P 500 and Nasdaq gains describe cap-weight benchmarks; they do not establish that equal-weight stocks or semiconductors have uniformly recovered.
findings.nextCheck: Compare SPX with RSP, SMH/QQQ, S5FI/S5TH and advance–decline readings for matched 10–12 November sessions.

findings.reason: The 10 November inflation surprise and reported bond-yield jump create a relevant alternative explanation to short-covering for the 11 November rebound; the mechanisms remain unproved without matched price/positioning data.
findings.sourceName: Reuters via MarketScreener — 10 November post-CPI tape
findings.nextCheck: Build event sequence and test US real yields, DXY, index intraday breadth and volume before attributing the bounce to positioning.

sweeps.title: Nvidia founder succession event: reported board consideration, not confirmed removal

findings.reason: The Wall Street Journal reports Nvidia's directors may consider removing Jensen Huang following a second reported affair, while Reuters says it could not independently verify the board's action. A board discussion is not a confirmed dismissal; founder succession is an additional valuation and execution risk, separate from observed GPU demand.
findings.sourceName: Reuters — reporting on WSJ board consideration, 11 November
findings.nextCheck: Read any new Nvidia original board statement, SEC 8-K or named transition plan; verify the separate investigation and next completed regular-session stock reaction.

findings.reason: Nvidia's original 8 November board statement expressed confidence in Huang and said it had no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised. That statement predates the newer 11 November reporting and cannot be represented as a fresh refutation.
findings.sourceName: Nvidia Investor Relations — board statement, 8 November
findings.nextCheck: Look for a subsequent original board statement after 11 November and distinguish findings from allegations.

findings.reason: Independent Nvidia directors publicly retained Joon H. Kim and Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate the reported foreign-intelligence targeting. The retention confirms an investigation, not an adverse finding or executive-removal decision.
findings.sourceName: Nvidia Investor Relations — independent directors' statement, 10 November
findings.nextCheck: Reconcile investigation findings with product guidance on 17 November, company leadership status and any new official export-control actions.

sweeps.title: Hot CPI meets Waller's explicit December policy fork

findings.reason: BLS reports October headline CPI +0.4% and core CPI +0.3% monthly; shelter rose +0.3%, food +0.5%, energy +0.7%. The normal October 12-month inflation comparison is unavailable because October 2025 data were not collected.
findings.sourceName: US Bureau of Labor Statistics — October CPI
findings.nextCheck: Check the underlying inflation components and November PPI; do not infer a missing year-on-year reading.

findings.reason: Waller said he would support a 25bp December hike even if inflation improved, and would consider 50bp if core CPI was around 0.3% or higher. Today's +0.3% core print meets his stated condition, but his position is not an FOMC decision.
findings.nextCheck: Compare subsequent Fed speakers, December futures pricing and official committee communication.

findings.reason: The October jobs report showed +165,000 nonfarm payrolls and 4.1% unemployment, yet long-term unemployment was 2.0 million (27.6% of unemployed): job creation and labour-market quality should be assessed separately.
findings.sourceName: US Bureau of Labor Statistics — October employment report
findings.nextCheck: Break out sector jobs, involuntary part-time work, wage growth and unemployment duration.

sweeps.title: TLT duration risk: stronger inflation versus the oil relief trade

findings.reason: Waller's 25bp December hike preference and conditional 50bp scenario create a rate-path risk to long-duration holdings such as TLT; this is a transmission hypothesis, not a verified change in TLT's price.
findings.nextCheck: Measure same-session 2Y/10Y/30Y nominal yields, real yields, TLT total return and curve steepening.

findings.reason: MarketWatch reported Treasury yields climbing after hot CPI. Treat the reported intraday move as a dated market reaction, not a closing print or proof that long-duration bonds are a buy.
findings.nextCheck: Read the matching timestamped Treasury yields and TLT prices, then check whether the selloff holds through the next full US session.

sweeps.title: AI cash conversion faces a higher-for-longer financing test

findings.reason: Waller explicitly cited AI-related high-tech equipment prices and electricity/energy pressures as potential persistent inflation contributors. AI demand may be strong while the cost of building it and financing it rises.
findings.nextCheck: Cross-check issuer capex, debt/lease commitments, free cash flow and the actual high-tech CPI/PPI subcomponents.

findings.reason: The Nvidia selloff/investigation story is principally a governance and key-person risk, not evidence that GPU shipments or AI demand have deteriorated. Its relation to operating economics requires a separate source check.
findings.sourceName: X Wire — ZeroHedge's Nvidia premarket report
findings.nextCheck: Check Nvidia primary disclosures, earnings guidance and dated share-price reactions; keep governance separate from hardware demand.

findings.reason: FX Evolution's earlier video advances a semiconductor deleveraging thesis. The technical and flow indicators discussed are attributed commentary, not independently verified market data.
findings.nextCheck: Compare actual SMH/QQQ relative returns, volume and attributable flow prints against reported claims.

sweeps.title: Iran de-escalation may reduce crude risk, not shipping constraints overnight

findings.reason: Reuters reports Trump is holding off additional Iran strikes while the US naval blockade of Hormuz remains. An apparent diplomatic improvement is not proof that navigation and deliveries have normalised.
findings.sourceName: Reuters — Iran strike pause and Gulf market reaction
findings.nextCheck: Check original government and maritime notices, sustained vessel crossings, insurance conditions and actual delivered barrels.

findings.reason: Waller warned that elevated transit and insurance costs and diesel/refining bottlenecks can transmit energy shocks to inflation even when tanker traffic partially returns. His cost assessment is not an independent physical-flow measurement.
findings.nextCheck: Test reported insurance/freight cost against UKMTO/AIS, refinery runs, diesel cracks and EIA stocks.

findings.reason: BLS reports October monthly energy CPI +0.7% after September's +5.2%; gasoline +1.0% after +9.1%. That moderation is backward-looking and cannot establish that November shipping costs have normalised.
findings.sourceName: US Bureau of Labor Statistics — October CPI
findings.nextCheck: Compare November fuel and physical shipping data; do not equate the dated CPI reading with a live oil-market quote.

sweeps.title: Two reviewed creators give opposite interpretations of AI-equity risk

findings.reason: TraderNick's November 9 video presents a tactical risk-on stance in equities and AI-capex beneficiaries. That is the creator's positioning and does not demonstrate measured breadth improvement.
findings.nextCheck: Check S&P 500 equal-weight, RSP, SMH and the share of stocks above 50D/200D averages at matching dates.

findings.reason: FX Evolution's earlier AI-bubble video argues that semiconductor and index selling could reflect concentrated deleveraging. These claims conflict with an uncomplicated risk-on interpretation and need price/flow verification.
findings.sourceName: FX Evolution — Wall Street Just Popped The AI Bubble?
findings.nextCheck: Compare SMH/QQQ price structure, options/flow datasets and retail-selling evidence before calling capitulation or recovery.
